Rule 18: a loose stick nest - random weave, wider than tall, open underneath - is not the saucer (a smooth wave brim), the dome (a close-weave half-sphere), the straight lantern, the slatted pear or the stepped drum. The weave itself is the distinction: every other piece in the range is an even lattice or straight slats. That is a 6% gap - every SKU on this listing sits about 6% under its list - which is a promotion rather than rounding, so RULE 22 makes the LIST price the cost basis and itemCostCad is 43.77, NOT 41.14. Contrast the pear, whose 1.4% gap was inside rule 22 and filed the sale figure. dutyRateBasis: Canada HS 9405.11.00 (electric lighting fittings designed for LED) / 9405.19.00 (other), MFN column, 7%. Canada applies no Section 301 equivalent to these goods - its surtaxes on Chinese imports cover electric vehicles, steel and aluminium - so MFN is the entire stack. The deeper difference from the US is the BASE: this 7% is charged on VALUE FOR DUTY, which is the supplier price, where the US charges its 41.4% (HTS 9405.11.80) on retail. About CA$2.04 a unit against US$40.57.
verdict: Priced at CA$84.99, CA$1.74 under the CA$86.73 RULE 2 ceiling (median CA$75.42 x 1.15). Contributes CA$23.69/unit on the wholesale basis (7% MFN on value for duty) at the LIST cost of C$43.77, against the CA$16.23 floor - clears by CA$7.46. Rule 22: the page sells at C$41.14, a 6% gap under the C$43.77 originalPrice, so the LIST price is the cost basis and the sale price is upside the model does not count.
